THE MECHANISM, and it is upstream of this project's router. ipykernel/iostream.py resolves a stream's parent header from a contextvars.ContextVar, falling back to a GLOBAL when unset. `threading.Thread` starts with an EMPTY context, so a background writer takes the global -- which holds whichever cell most recently set it, i.e. the LATER cell. The kernel itself stamps the straddling write with the later cell's msg_id, so the broker's router sees parent == sink.msg_id before idle and cannot separate it from the cell's own output. This matches R8-ipy13-experiment/EXPERIMENT.md's independent measurement of the same fact (a ContextVar is NOT inherited by a plain threading.Thread).

The fix, in this tree. The v1 defect is gone at the source: `pendingDrain` no longer exists as the coalescer (host.ts:408-418 documents the replacement by `drainLeaders`, a one-leader-per-run generation/dirty loop), and the target check now lives INSIDE one storage-domain update -- host.ts:1499 `if (held >= target)` inside the `this.runs().update(...)` transform at :1379, where the domain's per-run write chain serializes it against every other write. That is the same place the BUDGET check already was, which is why the sibling case CAP-09 never had this hole.

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL, and it reproduced v1's defect EXACTLY. Neutering the target check alone (host.ts:1499 -> `if (false && held >= target)`) did NOT restore the overshoot: admitted stayed 2, refused by the `mayAdmit` pre-check at host.ts:2150 instead. That is a real layering fact and it is recorded rather than hidden. Neutering BOTH layers (counting.ts:353 `return counts.capacityDeficit > 0` -> `return true`, plus the target check) restored the v1 signature byte-for-byte: [V8/CAP-10 measured] freedSlots=2 concurrentRequests=3 admitted=3 heldAgainstTarget3=4 deficitAfter=0, and the gate went red.
